placement.claim: A Git-backed review-artifact profile adjacent to proposal packets is the plausible first adapter over shared evidence-lineage semantics, but evidence has not resolved whether review-specific episode, outcome, finding, and synthesis semantics belong to proposal review or a shared cross-phase review capability.

reopening_conditions: Dogfooding shows that the shared evidence-lineage candidate cannot truthfully support both research claims and review findings, requiring a different dependency boundary.
A proposal revision exercises reviewer episodes, finding-level applicability, truthful empty or failure outcomes, conflict preservation, and synthesis reference integrity.
An implementation-review consumer establishes review-specific lifecycle requirements that make a proposal-local profile incorrect.
Observed review remediation requires transactional or runtime semantics that Git-backed artifacts cannot provide.
A concrete consumer shows that selection, findings, synthesis, and resolution require different durable owners.

authority.decision_owner: user or future explicitly authorized portfolio owner

relationships.rationale: Review artifacts causally require statement identity, evidence baseline, provenance, sensitivity, authority-scope, and lineage semantics. They consume this candidate only if it is selected as the shared owner; another valid owner must provide equivalent consequences if dogfooding rejects that placement.

Adaptive coordination needs a durable way to bind findings and synthesis to an exact subject revision and preserve later applicability; this semantic dependency does not impose a mandatory delivery order.
